notes.title: Next update
notes.notes:
It has been a long time, and I know this is just a joke of a game. But I am still working on it. I've been working on a couple new game projects that are actual real games (as well as other work because money is required to live). However I do plan on finishing up the next big update real soon. I will also be moving the game out of early access as there isn't much else I can do with it beyond make new maps. Which is what I plan on doing. It will be out of early access but i'll continue to make new content for it because it's a fun chill game to work on.

So yeah this isn't an abandon game, life just got in the way but it's still very much on my to do list. My next game will also have online multiplayer, if I can figure that out i'll see about eventually making the multiplayer "go outside together" update.

notes.title: Update 0.6 No longer indestructible.
notes.notes:
New update, it feels small, but it's a lot of groundwork for the next update. One thing that has been added is interactivity. I've finally started adding the ability to interact with things in different ways. It's very basic right now but more stuff will be added. One thing this adds is new secrets to find in each environment. Easter eggs may not always be passive anymore.

However be warned, as the title suggests the outdoors are a bit more dangerous. [b]The ability to die is now present.[/b]

No lives or health bars, so your exploration can still be calm and relaxing. But if you die your walk in that environment ends. 

So go out and explore, find new things, look for secrets. More secrets, more interactivity, and more amusing ways to end your walks will be added. Also I'm still trying to figure out multiplayer, I have not given up on that.

Change log:
[list]
[*] Added death
[*] Interactivity overhaul
[*] Added first secret environment (you will need to find it)
[*] Texture update Mars
[*] Texture update Island

notes.title: Next update incoming
notes.notes:
Although I don't always have time for this game I am always picking away at it and thinking of new ways to improve it. To that end the next update will have some improvements and a new gameplay feature that will enhance the outside experience. No spoilers but it will be a simple yet amusing addition.

Also I've been learning about implementing multiplayer in a new project I've been working on, and if it works I will also be implementing multiplayer in Go Outside Simulator. There are lots of Easter eggs to find on every map, with more planned to be added. A friend or 2 might make finding them easier and/or funner.

Finally I still have no plans to increase the price so continue to enjoy the outdoors for only $0.99 USD while also helping me fund this and future projects. Everyone who has taken the time to play this is the real MVP and I thank you.

notes.title: About the new environment in the latest update
notes.notes:
Ok I pushed an update for the first time in a year. It's mostly just small fixes and improvements. I also tossed in the new map I've been working on. It's horrifically broken.

Play it as you can because i'm probably removing it in the next update and will not put it back in until it's not horrifically broken. Like if you play that map, then go to the main menu and play another map, the controller in that map will be broken and gravity will screw up. It's actually kind of funny so have fun playing with that. Restarting the game fixes it and everything else works as well as it did before. So just be warned you will need to restart the game after you leave the cylinder if you want to play other maps.

So yeah, it's in temporarily, I will be pulling it with the next update and it will not return until it is no longer making me cry.

notes.title: Next Update
notes.notes:
I know very few people actually care about this project but I am still working on it. I’m actually very surprised and pleased to see how well it has gone considering its 50% joke and 50% learning experience. All that being said the next update will be a big one and will likely push it out of early access. Although it will be out of early access I will continue to work on it as time goes on. Right now I’ve been in pre development of my next project which will be a real game and not just a basic looking joke. However I won’t start to work on that in Unity until GOS is out of early access. 

The next update will polish some functions, fix problems, add more set dressing and will include a new and rather strange environment. I have tons of ideas for new environments and places to build and as I generally improve I will update the game. Even if I’m working on other projects and am far removed from GOS I will continue to update it as time goes on because if nothing else it’s a fun stupid project.

Thank you all who have played the game, even if you refunded it right after I hope you at least got some amusement out of the concept or finding the Easter eggs. Once I finish the next update I will begin full work on my next project but will not stop adding to GOS. Also I would like to say the price will not change, I had thought about bumping it up a little once it leaves early access but I won’t. I want it to stay cheap and honestly charging more for what it is feels like a crime. Sure I’ve put a lot of work and time into it but I didn’t make it for money so it will remain a cheap gag you can waste time in. That being said the support does help and I’m shocked I got as many purchases as I did. 

Onward and upward.

notes.title: Development update
notes.notes:
It's been a little while since the last update, This was mostly because the computer in which it was being worked on needed to get it's graphics card replaced so it has been out of commission for the last few weeks. Computer is back and development can continue. 

However it's not perfectly smooth sailing. After updating to the most recent version of Unity a few things broke and are in the process of being fixed. Nothing was lost or anything, just updating stuff and fixing broken scrips. The pause menu was one casualty, I may fix it or just scrap it and implement a better less garbage one (which I’ve been planning to do anyway) so we will see how that pans out.

Anyway all that aside development will pick back up and updates can be expected in the near future. In my computers down time I’ve been looking into procedural generation for another project I want to work on in the future. The best way to toy with it would be to use it in GOS and see how it works. If I do add procedural generation it will be in a dedicated level and not in all levels. The environments are all made to be a static size and static configuration, however it might be fun to add one or more procedural environments for those who want to walk forever. No ETA on that feature and I don’t want to make promises I can’t keep, but I am looking into it so it may happen. I have also looked at suggestion made in the discussions and will work on a few, no guarantees on multiplayer (it would be kind of funny not going to lie) but proper controller support will likely happen.

Thank you for supporting Go Outside Simulator and thank you to everyone who’s left a review, I’m pleased to see people either got the joke or genuinely enjoy the concept.
